raw_response:
I will keep to the usual pattern that fits my age, my experience, and the conditions in Quzhou County: a wheat-maize rotation as the main line, with most of my land staying in grain. I would not make big risky changes. Wheat and summer maize are familiar, easy to sell, and match the local climate, irrigation habits, and machinery. At the start of the growing season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will manage it carefully with one topdressing of nitrogen, irrigation at the key stages if water is available, and disease and insect control only when pressure is clear. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize quickly to catch heat and moisture, use hybrid seed for stable yield, apply most fertilizer up front with some nitrogen reserved for later growth, and irrigate mainly at the critical stages if rain is not enough. I will use rotary tillage for convenience and cost control on most plots. I want a steady harvest more than a complicated plan, so I will stay with grain crops, moderate inputs, and practical field management I can handle well.
